sandhi.note: The m of सर्वम् joins the following vowel; the m of आपोमयम् becomes anusvāra before j.

sandhi.type: visarga sandhi inside a derived word
sandhi.note: The nominative plural आपः keeps its ending before the suffix -मय, and -aḥ before m becomes -o, as between words.

morph.note: -मय ‘consisting of, full of’ is normally added to a stem (अप् would give अम्मय or अप्मय). आपोमय is built on the plural आपः itself — an old formation also found in Vedic prose. ‘The whole world (was) water’.
Past participle of वञ्चय- (causative of √वञ्च्, ‘cause to go astray’, i.e. deceive), instrumental dual: the two asuras, ‘deceived’ by the boon they had granted.

mantras.anvaya: इति वञ्चिताभ्यां (ताभ्यां) तदा सर्वं जगत् आपोमयं (विलोक्य) —
mantras.anvaya_en: A participial agent phrase and the object of an absolutive; the absolutive विलोक्य and the passive verb गदितः come in 1.101.
mantras.lit: By the two, thus deceived, then — the whole world (being) made of water —
mantras.tr: Thus deceived, the two then looked and saw the whole world turned to water,
mantras.tr_note: ‘Looked and saw’ is supplied from विलोक्य at the start of 1.101; the instrumental agent is rendered as the subject.

comm.t: The asuras realise they have been caught by their own word. Looking about for a way out, they see that the whole world is water — the cosmic flood on which Viṣṇu slept (1.66–67).

Who deceived them is left implicit: by Viṣṇu’s taking them at their word, and behind that by Mahāmāyā, who had bewildered them (1.94). The narrative makes the deception the Goddess’s work, done through the god.

samasa.literal: he whose eyes are like lotuses

morph.note: Imperative second singular of √हन्: before the ending -हि the root is replaced by ज- (ज + हि → जहि). The asuras still speak as if commanding.
Past passive participle of √गद् with the connecting vowel -इ-: ‘(was) spoken to’. The person addressed is the subject (भगवान्), the speakers the agent (ताभ्याम्).
Absolutive in -य after the prefix वि-. Its agent is the instrumental ताभ्याम्, the agent of the passive main verb — a regular construction.

mantras.anvaya: (सर्वम् आपोमयं जगत्) विलोक्य ताभ्यां कमलेक्षणः भगवान् गदितः — ‘यत्र उर्वी सलिलेन परिप्लुता न (अस्ति, तत्र) आवां जहि।’
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line completes 1.100 with a passive main verb (गदितः); the second is the asuras’ words, a command with a relative clause of place (यत्र … न).
mantras.lit: having looked, the lotus-eyed Blessed One was addressed by the two: ‘Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water.’
mantras.tr: and they said to the lotus-eyed Lord, “Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water.”
mantras.tr_note: The passive (‘was addressed by the two’) is rendered actively.

comm.t: The asuras try to slip their promise: since the whole world is water, a place ‘where the earth is not flooded’ seems not to exist. They grant the boon on a condition they think cannot be met.

The Purāṇa recension (the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa as edited in GRETIL) has further lines after this verse that the Gita Press text does not carry; this edition follows the Gita Press 700 and adds nothing (see corrections.json, recension notes).

comm.t: A second ‘the seer said’ only two verses after the first (1.99): the Gita Press pāṭha marks the return to narration after the asuras’ quoted words. Medhas tells the end of the fight.

samasa.vigraha: शङ्खः च चक्रं च गदा च शङ्खचक्रगदाः; ताः बिभर्ति इति शङ्खचक्रगदाभृत्, तेन
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa containing an itaretara dvandva (शङ्खचक्रगदा)
samasa.literal: by the bearer of conch, discus and mace
samasa.sense: by Viṣṇu, named by his emblems; -भृत् is √भृ ‘to bear’ with the zero kṛt affix (kvip) and an added t

morph.note: Past participle of √छिद्: after the root’s final d the t of the suffix becomes n and the d becomes n too (छिद् + त → छिन्न). Neuter dual -ए, agreeing with शिरसी: ‘the two heads were cut off’.
Absolutive of √वच् with samprasāraṇa (व → उ) and k for c: उक्त्वा ‘having said’. With कृत्वा it gives two steps before the main act.

Neuter dual of शिरस्: nominative and accusative are the same (शिरसी), so the one word serves both as the object of कृत्वा (‘having placed their heads’) and the subject of छिन्ने (‘the heads were cut off’). A neuter dual in -ī (like छिन्ने in -e) is pragṛhya and would stand unjoined before a vowel (ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम्, 1.1.11); here a consonant follows, so no question of sandhi arises.

mantras.anvaya: ‘तथा’ इति उक्त्वा, शङ्खचक्रगदाभृता भगवता तयोः शिरसी जघने कृत्वा चक्रेण वै छिन्ने।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive sentence: the subject शिरसी with its verb छिन्ने, the agent भगवता, and two absolutives (उक्त्वा, कृत्वा) sharing that agent. शिरसी does double duty as the object of कृत्वा.
mantras.lit: Having said ‘So (be it)’, by the Blessed One, bearer of conch, discus and mace, having placed (them) on (his) loins, the two heads of the two were indeed cut off with the discus.
mantras.tr: Saying “So be it,” the Lord who bears the conch, the discus and the mace laid them on his lap and cut off their two heads with his discus.
mantras.tr_note: The passive is rendered actively. जघन, properly the hips or loins, is rendered ‘lap’: the one place above the water.

comm.t: Viṣṇu meets the condition exactly: the only ground not covered by water is his own body. He lays their heads on his lap and cuts them off with the discus. The asuras die by the terms of their own boon.

The narrative turns the asuras’ cleverness against them, as the boon itself was turned (1.97). The cause, as the chapter has insisted, is Mahāmāyā’s delusion rather than force: five thousand years of fighting did not end the war, a confusion of mind did.
A modern reflection: the asuras look for a loophole in the world and find none outside the one they are fighting. The story leaves no place that is not within the Lord’s reach.

sandhi.note: -āḥ before a voiced sound loses its visarga (अस्या देव्याः); before t the visarga becomes s (देव्यास्तु).
Before ś the visarga may stay or become ś; the text keeps the visarga.

morph.note: Past participle of सम् + उद् + √पद्: d + t → nn (पद् + त → पन्न). Used as a finite verb: ‘(she) arose’. The word picks up उत्पन्ना of 1.66.
Imperative of √श्रु (svādi): the root becomes शृ- before the class sign -नु, which becomes -णु after ṛ; the ending -हि is dropped after the u of the class sign.
Present tense used for the immediate future: ‘I am going to tell you’. Medhas announces the next story (chapters 2–4).

mantras.anvaya: एवम् एषा (देवी) स्वयं ब्रह्मणा संस्तुता समुत्पन्ना। अस्याः देव्याः प्रभावं तु भूयः शृणु, (अहं) ते वदामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: A closing summary (एवम् … समुत्पन्ना), then the transition to the next story: an imperative and a first-person present.
mantras.lit: Thus she arose, praised by Brahmā himself. But hear further the power of this Goddess; I tell (it) to you.
mantras.tr: So it was that she appeared, praised by Brahmā himself. Now hear more of this Goddess’s power; I shall tell you.
mantras.tr_note: स्वयम् is taken with ब्रह्मणा (‘by Brahmā himself’). It can also be taken with the subject: ‘she appeared of her own accord’.

comm.t: Medhas closes the first story and opens the next. The ring is complete: he had said that the eternal Goddess is called ‘born’ (उत्पन्ना) when she appears for the gods’ purpose (1.65–66); now he says एवम् एषा समुत्पन्ना — ‘this is how she arose’. शृणु and ते are singular: he speaks to the king.

This is the last mantra of chapter 1. In the Gita Press pāṭha it is followed by the bījas ऐं ॐ, closing the sampuṭa that ॐ ऐं opened in 1.1; they belong to the recitation, not to the Purāṇa. The colophon names the chapter मधुकैटभवधः, the Slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the first carita, which the pāṭha assigns to Mahākālī.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has a name for a goddess praised by the gods, 83 ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवसंस्तुतवैभवा, ‘whose glory is praised by Brahmā, Upendra, Mahendra and the other gods’. The motif is shared; the Devī Māhātmya has just told one such praise in full.

flags.uncertain: स्वयम् may qualify ब्रह्मणा (‘by Brahmā himself’, chosen) or the Goddess (‘she arose of her own accord’); both readings are grammatical.
